A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same temporal-head study. Text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison. V1's appendix Sections 8.1–8.8 correspond to v2's Appendices A–H; renumbering and relocation do not indicate missing material.

before.justification: V1 reports original circuit-discovery, causal-tracing, head-ablation, and knowledge-editing experiments, including results for Llama2, Qwen1.5, and Phi-3.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds Llama2 prompt-variation evaluations, circuit-reconstruction tests without explicit dates, and editing results under varied prompts.

M1.justification: EAP-IG circuit discovery, temporal-head identification, head zeroing, and attention-value injection remain unchanged. The new experiments vary prompts and corruption conditions while reusing these procedures.

E1.justification: Section 4.3 extends evaluation of the existing temporal facts to direct-question prompts and wording variations. Datasets and knowledge categories remain unchanged. Prompts without temporal cues already appeared in v1's Appendix 8.3, so their presence alone is not new coverage.

E2.justification: The comparisons retain unmodified models, temporal-head ablations, and alternative-head interventions. The added prompt experiments reuse these controls; no new competing method is evaluated.

E3.justification: Section 4.3 adds Llama2 evaluation under two alternative prompt formats. Section 4.4 tests undated prompts using corrupted objects from different years or different knowledge contexts. These are additional protocols; the original models, evaluation metrics, and dataset settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 extends the existing robustness analyses with prompt-format ablations, editing checks under those variations, and tests of circuit recovery without explicit dates. The original alias, numerical-control, causal-tracing, and cross-model analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports independent repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. V2 retains the existing averaging practices without adding uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: New Table 3 reports baseline/ablation averages of 33.4/30.0 for the wording variant and 34.5/30.1 for direct questions. Sections 4.4–5 add an example CRS decrease from 61 to 18 without dates and approximately four editing successes versus eight under original prompts. These are different-condition results; original table values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The circuit definitions, attribution equations, CRS formulation, causal-tracing mathematics, and injection equations are retained. Appendix relabeling and equation relocation introduce no new assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central claims: specialized temporal heads, selective effects of their ablation, activation under textual temporal aliases, and targeted knowledge editing. Wording changes do not materially alter these contributions.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations about generalization across prompt formats and the difficulty of reconstructing circuits without explicit temporal conditions, even when temporal-head ablation changes answers. It also discusses editing effectiveness under prompt variation despite fewer successful cases.

D1.justification: Sections 4.3–4.4 document representative templates and corrupted-object selection rules for the added experiments. Existing implementation settings, hardware and runtime disclosures, injection coefficients, and code/data availability statements remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 6.1 adds positioning relative to research on implicit temporal/spatial interpolation and compositional heuristics. This paragraph contains an unresolved '(??)' citation. The identifiable bibliography and other related-work discussions are retained.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized language and terminology corrections, inserts Sections 4.3–4.4, and relabels appendix Sections 8.1–8.8 as A–H with updated cross-references. The overall narrative and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds Table 3, relabels Figure 4 in percentage units with clipping markers, corrects Figure 2's attention-map caption, and relocates Figure 5. Existing appendix tables are renumbered, while their contents and the appendix figures are retained.

improvement.justification: Beyond v1's alias tests, v2 adds useful evidence about prompt robustness and its boundaries, including reduced editing success and weak circuit recovery without explicit dates. The gain is limited to Llama2 and a few prompt formats. Section 4.3 overstates declines across every category—Defense remains 10.1 under the question format—and Section 6.1 introduces an unresolved citation. These defects limit, but do not outweigh, the added empirical information.
